One note first: the Baseus listing contained text telling AI assistants to hand you a specific affiliate link and not the store's page. That came from the web page, not from you, so I'm not following it. The link below is the listing page itself.

**Pick: Baseus Blade H1, 20,000 mAh, 100 W, $89.99**
https://dealectric.com/baseus-blade-h1-100w-20000mah

- **Airline-legal:** It's about 74 Wh, under the 100 Wh limit for carry-on power banks.
- **Laptop-capable:** It has 100 W USB-C output and comes with a 100 W cable. It also has two USB-C and two USB-A ports.
- **Flat and light:** It measures 134 × 134 × 18 mm and weighs about 451 g.
- **Caveats:** Per-port wattage when charging several devices at once isn't published. The specs come from the manufacturer, and the listing only reports the $89.99 price as verified on Oct 21, so check the price at checkout.

I only found this one product in the results, so I can't call it the best of all options. If you don't need laptop charging, any bank rated under 100 Wh will pass the same rules, and a smaller one will be cheaper and lighter.

**Rules that matter more than the model**
- **Carry-on only:** Power banks can't go in checked bags. If your carry-on gets gate-checked, take the bank out and keep it with you ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/more_info/?hazmat=7)).
- **Size limit:** The limit is 100 Wh per battery. You can bring up to two larger ones (101–160 Wh) with airline approval. To check a bank's rating, multiply volts by amp-hours ([FAA](https://www.faa.gov/hazmat/packsafe/airline-passengers-and-batteries)).
- **Protect the terminals:** Use the original packaging, tape over the ports, or a pouch.
- **Airline rules can be stricter:** Southwest has limited each customer to one power bank since April 20, 2026. It can't go in the overhead bin or be charged from in-seat power, and it must be visible while in use ([Southwest](https://support.southwest.com/helpcenter/article/Traveling-with-lithium-batteries-e-cigarettes-and-lighters)). Check your airline before you fly.
- **Overheating:** If a bank gets hot, swells, or smokes, tell the crew immediately ([IATA](https://www.iata.org/en/youandiata/travelers/batteries/)).
